_comment: The four reference sets for Part 2. Each one exists to stress a different axis of the
renderer, so they are not interchangeable and a capture is not 'done' because one of them
landed. Status is recorded per set and is the honest state, not the intent.

targets.why: A histogram with a colorer plot and a hidden moving average — the smallest thing that exercises per-bar colour selection, a non-price pane, and a plot that carries values while not being drawn.

targets.what: 'Uncharted Clouds' — the firm's own Pine script
targets.why: Twenty-one hidden layer plots that exist only as fill anchors, plus two moving averages. It is the script that proved lenient `ok:true` was a lie for a hosting caller, so it is the natural stress case for fills, z-order and hidden-plot handling.
targets.blocked: Not present on the capture layout. It lives on the owner's own chart; adding it mutates a saved layout, so it is left for an authorised pass.

sets.why: The baseline. Daily bars, a liquid symbol, enough history that no plot is inside its warmup.

status.screenshots: not captured — the capture layout carries another session's probe study, so a screenshot of it is not a clean reference for anything

sets.why: A second symbol at the same timeframe, so a difference between A and B is about the DATA and never about the timeframe.
Weekly. Changes bar spacing and the time axis without changing the symbol, which is where x-coordinate and label-collision bugs surface.
Intraday 4H. Sessions, gaps and a non-continuous time axis — the case where a renderer that assumes evenly spaced bars finally breaks.
